examples.ja: その教師は講堂に学生を集めた。
examples.en: The teacher assembled the students in the hall.
examples.furigana: その{教師|きょうし}は{講堂|こうどう}に{学生|がくせい}を{集|あつ}めた。

examples.ja: ぼくたちが講堂に入るとすぐ式が始まった。
examples.en: No sooner had we entered the hall than the ceremony began.
examples.furigana: ぼくたちが{講堂|こうどう}に{入|はい}るとすぐ{式|しき}が{始|はじ}まった。

mnemonic: A {bird} with a boxy eye on top and four tail feathers flickering like flames below; a ~Chow Chow dog~ leaps, snaps the feathers off and spits them out. A ^Tory^ parrot, the bird's friend, squawks at the dog (とり).

vocab.mnemonic: Built from 小 (little, こ) + 鳥 (bird, とり): a {small bird}.

examples.ja: 小鳥たちはたのしそうにさえずっています。
examples.en: The birds are singing merrily.
examples.furigana: {小鳥|ことり}たちはたのしそうにさえずっています。

examples.ja: 小鳥たちが木の上でないていた。
examples.en: Birds were singing up in the tree.
examples.furigana: {小鳥|ことり}たちが{木|き}の{上|うえ}でないていた。

mnemonic: You [eat] a {meal} in ^messy^ (めし) gulps, [anti-] every table manner, so rice sprays everywhere; ~Han Solo~ blasts the last grain off your chopsticks.
A mud-splattered ~Bento box~ won't accept any [excuse] on the left: it flexes a [power] arm on the right and makes you do push-ups before lunch: {study hard}, no excuses!

In {winter}, your [walking legs] up top hit two slick patches of [ice] below and shoot out from under you; you land on your tailbone, teeth rattling. '^Phew, you!^' he gasps at his friend, sliding across the winter ice (ふゆ).

~Chewbacca~ blows a [bamboo flute] so loud from above that the sun at [sunrise] below leaps straight up into full {daytime}; the whole town wakes screaming. A ^Hero^ in a cape lifts the sun up to noon (ひる).

meanings_id: waktu dari matahari terbit hingga terbenam
vocab.mnemonic: Built from 昼 (daytime, ひる) + 間 (interval, ま): the interval of daytime, {during the day}.

examples.ja: フクロウは昼間は目が見えない。
examples.en: Owls cannot see in the daytime.
examples.furigana: フクロウは{昼間|ひるま}は{目|め}が{見|み}えない。

examples.ja: 昼間、友人が私に会いに来た。
examples.en: A friend of mine came to see me during the day.
examples.furigana: {昼間|ひるま}、{友人|ゆうじん}が{私|わたし}に{会|あ}いに{来|き}た。

vocab.mnemonic: Built from 昼 (ひる, daytime) + 休み (やすみ, rest): {lunch break}.

examples.ja: お昼休みは、１時間です。
examples.en: Lunch break is an hour long.

examples.ja: 12時から1時まで、1時間の昼休みがある。
examples.en: We have an hour's recess for lunch from twelve to one.

mnemonic: [flowers] bloom on top of an [umbrella] stuck in a [tree] below. ~Charlie Chaplin~ shakes the trunk, and petals rain into his cup to brew {tea}. He sips, twirls his cane, and burns his mustache.

meanings_id: pengabdian setia kepada yang lebih tua
mnemonic: My {younger brother} wears plastic [horns] on top, ties himself up in a [bow] string, and a [walking stick] skewers the knot; a mud-splattered ~Dinosaur~ carries him off, wailing. An ^Otter-toad^ copies my little brother, horns and all (おとうと).

A {cow} with one horn poking up through its head spins on ice. ~Figure skater~ twirls it by that horn, faster and faster, until it sprays milk across the rink. The skater gasps '^Ooh, shoes!^' and laces on ice skates shaped like cow hooves (うし).

A {fish} is [bound up (small)] by the head, its scales scored into a [rice field] grid, roasting over an [oven fire]. ~Gyoro~ watches from her bowl, goggle eyes bulging in horror. A ^Sock-can-ah^: the fish is wrapped in a sock in a can (さかな).

A huge [mouth] on top of skinny [human legs]: your {elder brother}, bragging nonstop. ~Kyoto Geisha~ kneels to pour his tea, and he shouts orders until she flings it in his face. His sister ^Annie^ rolls her eyes as he brags (あに).
A [St. Bernard dog] flings one [drop] of drool from its top-right ear onto ~Ken doll~'s perfect hair: the ultimate {dog}. An ^Inuit^ (いぬ) musher laughs and hitches it to his sled.

A tiny [woman] on the left who's [not yet] grown: your {younger sister}. ~Mime~ silently copies her every pout until she bursts into tears, and you get blamed. An ^Emo-toad^ copies her pouting too (いもうと).

My bossy {elder sister}, a [woman] on the left, storms through the [market] on the right, piling every bag onto a staggering ~Sheep~ until its knees buckle. The sheep collapses, braying '^Ah, nay!^': no more bags (あね).
Pour [water] from the left onto [Chinese clay] and you get mud for carving {Chinese} characters; a ~Kangaroo~ stamps kanji into it with her tail, splattering everyone.
